# `<sl-dialog>` — Dialog

> **Customized in Saipem DS.** It differs from upstream Shoelace: new attribute `variant` ('default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'); new CSS part `status-icon`. Use only the API below.

Dialogs, sometimes called "modals", appear above the page and require the user's immediate attention.

**Status:** stable · **Since:** 2.0

**Import:** `import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/dialog/dialog.js';`

**Uses internally (registered automatically):** `<sl-icon>`, `<sl-icon-button>`

## Attributes

Every attribute is also a property (camelCase name in the second column when it differs). Boolean attributes are on when present: never write `="false"`, remove the attribute or bind the property instead.

| Attribute | Property | Type / allowed values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | — | `boolean` | `false` | Indicates whether or not the dialog is open. You can toggle this attribute to show and hide the dialog, or you can use the `show()` and `hide()` methods and this attribute will reflect the dialog's open state. |
| `label` | — | `string` | `''` | The dialog's label as displayed in the header. You should always include a relevant label even when using `no-header`, as it is required for proper accessibility. If you need to display HTML, use the `label` slot instead. |
| `no-header` | `noHeader` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the header. This will also remove the default close button, so please ensure you provide an easy, accessible way for users to dismiss the dialog. |
| `variant` | — | `default`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `'default'` | The dialog's status. `success`, `warning` and `danger` show a matching icon before the title, for confirmations and outcomes; `default` shows none. The footer buttons are not changed: pick their variants in the `footer` slot. |

## Properties without an attribute

These can only be set from JavaScript: `element.prop = value`, `[prop]="value"` in Angular, `.prop=${value}` in Lit. Writing them as HTML attributes does nothing.

| Property | Type | Notes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modal` | — |  | Exposes the internal modal utility that controls focus trapping. To temporarily disable focus trapping and allow third-party modals spawned from an active Shoelace modal, call `modal.activateExternal()` when the third-party modal opens. Upon closing, call `modal.deactivateExternal()` to restore Shoelace's focus trapping. |

## Events

Listen with `addEventListener`, `(event-name)` in Angular or `@event-name` in Lit. Data is on `event.detail`.

| Event | `event.detail` | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sl-show` | — | Emitted when the dialog opens. |
| `sl-after-show` | — | Emitted after the dialog opens and all animations are complete. |
| `sl-hide` | — | Emitted when the dialog closes. |
| `sl-after-hide` | — | Emitted after the dialog closes and all animations are complete. |
| `sl-initial-focus` | — | Emitted when the dialog opens and is ready to receive focus. Calling `event.preventDefault()` will prevent focusing and allow you to set it on a different element, such as an input. |
| `sl-request-close` | `{ source: 'close-button' \| 'keyboard' \| 'overlay' }` | Emitted when the user attempts to close the dialog by clicking the close button, clicking the overlay, or pressing escape. Calling `event.preventDefault()` will keep the dialog open. Avoid using this unless closing the dialog will result in destructive behavior such as data loss. |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `show()` | Shows the dialog. |
| `hide()` | Hides the dialog |

## Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| (default) | The dialog's main content. |
| `label` | The dialog's label. Alternatively, you can use the `label` attribute. |
| `header-actions` | Optional actions to add to the header. Works best with `<sl-icon-button>`. |
| `footer` | The dialog's footer, usually one or more buttons representing various options. |

## CSS parts

Parts exist for fine adjustments. Do not use them to change colours, borders or fonts: a missing look is a missing variant of the DS.

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `base` | The component's base wrapper. |
| `overlay` | The overlay that covers the screen behind the dialog. |
| `panel` | The dialog's panel (where the dialog and its content are rendered). |
| `header` | The dialog's header. This element wraps the title and header actions. |
| `header-actions` | Optional actions to add to the header. Works best with `<sl-icon-button>`. |
| `title` | The dialog's title. |
| `status-icon` | The status icon shown before the title when `variant` is not `default`. |
| `close-button` | The close button, an `<sl-icon-button>`. |
| `close-button__base` | The close button's exported `base` part. |
| `body` | The dialog's body. |
| `footer` | The dialog's footer. |

## CSS custom properties

| Property | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--width` | — | The preferred width of the dialog. Note that the dialog will shrink to accommodate smaller screens. |
| `--header-spacing` | — | The amount of padding to use for the header. |
| `--body-spacing` | — | The amount of padding to use for the body. |
| `--footer-spacing` | — | The amount of padding to use for the footer. |

## Documentation and examples

<!-- cspell:dictionaries lorem-ipsum -->

```html
<sl-dialog label="Dialog" class="dialog-overview">
  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
  <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Close</sl-button>
</sl-dialog>

<sl-button>Open Dialog</sl-button>

<script>
  const dialog = document.querySelector('.dialog-overview');
  const openButton = dialog.nextElementSibling;
  const closeButton = dialog.querySelector('sl-button[slot="footer"]');

  openButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.hide());
</script>
```

```ts
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/button/button.js';
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/dialog/dialog.js';
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dialog-example',
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <sl-dialog label="Dialog" [open]="open()" (sl-after-hide)="open.set(false)">
      Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary" (click)="open.set(false)">Close</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-button (click)="open.set(true)">Open Dialog</sl-button>
  `
})
export class DialogExampleComponent {
  // Bind `open` rather than calling show()/hide(): the dialog also closes on its own (close button, overlay,
  // Escape), so listen for sl-after-hide to keep the signal in step with the element.
  readonly open = signal(false);
}
```

## Examples

### Variants

Use the `variant` attribute to mark a confirmation or an outcome. `success`, `warning` and `danger` show a status icon
before the title; `default` shows none. The footer buttons keep their own variants: a destructive confirmation uses a
`danger` primary action.

```html
<div class="dialog-variants">
  <sl-dialog label="Return to working" variant="warning">
    Do you want to return 2026-BID-000003 to the Working state?
    <sl-button slot="footer">Cancel</sl-button>
    <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Return to working</sl-button>
  </sl-dialog>
  <sl-dialog label="Bid deleted" variant="success">
    2026-BID-000003 has been deleted.
    <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Close</sl-button>
  </sl-dialog>
  <sl-dialog label="Delete bid" variant="danger">
    2026-BID-000003 and its attachments will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
    <sl-button slot="footer">Cancel</sl-button>
    <sl-button slot="footer" variant="danger">Delete bid</sl-button>
  </sl-dialog>

  <sl-button data-variant="warning">Warning</sl-button>
  <sl-button data-variant="success">Success</sl-button>
  <sl-button data-variant="danger">Danger</sl-button>
</div>

<script>
  const container = document.querySelector('.dialog-variants');

  container.querySelectorAll('sl-button[data-variant]').forEach(button => {
    const dialog = container.querySelector(`sl-dialog[variant="${button.dataset.variant}"]`);
    button.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
    dialog.querySelectorAll('sl-button[slot="footer"]').forEach(b => b.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.hide()));
  });
</script>
```

```ts
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/button/button.js';
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/dialog/dialog.js';
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA, signal } from '@angular/core';

type DialogVariant = 'warning' | 'success' | 'danger';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dialog-variants-example',
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <sl-dialog
      label="Return to working"
      variant="warning"
      [open]="openVariant() === 'warning'"
      (sl-after-hide)="close()"
    >
      Do you want to return 2026-BID-000003 to the Working state?
      <sl-button slot="footer" (click)="close()">Cancel</sl-button>
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary" (click)="close()">Return to working</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-dialog label="Bid deleted" variant="success" [open]="openVariant() === 'success'" (sl-after-hide)="close()">
      2026-BID-000003 has been deleted.
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary" (click)="close()">Close</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-dialog label="Delete bid" variant="danger" [open]="openVariant() === 'danger'" (sl-after-hide)="close()">
      2026-BID-000003 and its attachments will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
      <sl-button slot="footer" (click)="close()">Cancel</sl-button>
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="danger" (click)="close()">Delete bid</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-button (click)="openVariant.set('warning')">Warning</sl-button>
    <sl-button (click)="openVariant.set('success')">Success</sl-button>
    <sl-button (click)="openVariant.set('danger')">Danger</sl-button>
  `
})
export class DialogVariantsExampleComponent {
  readonly openVariant = signal<DialogVariant | null>(null);

  close() {
    this.openVariant.set(null);
  }
}
```

### Scrolling

By design, a dialog's height will never exceed that of the viewport. As such, dialogs will not scroll with the page ensuring the header and footer are always accessible to the user.

```html
<sl-dialog label="Dialog" class="dialog-scrolling">
  <div style="height: 150vh; border: dashed 2px var(--sl-color-neutral-200); padding: 0 1rem;">
    <p>Scroll down and give it a try! 👇</p>
  </div>
  <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Close</sl-button>
</sl-dialog>

<sl-button>Open Dialog</sl-button>

<script>
  const dialog = document.querySelector('.dialog-scrolling');
  const openButton = dialog.nextElementSibling;
  const closeButton = dialog.querySelector('sl-button[slot="footer"]');

  openButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.hide());
</script>
```

}

### Header Actions

The header shows a functional close button by default. You can use the `header-actions` slot to add additional [icon buttons](icon-button.md) if needed.

```html
<sl-dialog label="Dialog" class="dialog-header-actions">
  <sl-icon-button class="new-window" slot="header-actions" name="box-arrow-up-right"></sl-icon-button>
  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
  <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Close</sl-button>
</sl-dialog>

<sl-button>Open Dialog</sl-button>

<script>
  const dialog = document.querySelector('.dialog-header-actions');
  const openButton = dialog.nextElementSibling;
  const closeButton = dialog.querySelector('sl-button[slot="footer"]');
  const newWindowButton = dialog.querySelector('.new-window');

  openButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.hide());
  newWindowButton.addEventListener('click', () => window.open(location.href));
</script>
```

```ts
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/button/button.js';
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/dialog/dialog.js';
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/icon-button/icon-button.js';
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dialog-header-actions-example',
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <sl-dialog label="Dialog" [open]="open()" (sl-after-hide)="open.set(false)">
      <sl-icon-button slot="header-actions" name="box-arrow-up-right" (click)="openInNewWindow()"></sl-icon-button>
      Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary" (click)="open.set(false)">Close</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-button (click)="open.set(true)">Open Dialog</sl-button>
  `
})
export class DialogHeaderActionsExampleComponent {
  readonly open = signal(false);

  openInNewWindow() {
    window.open(location.href);
  }
}
```

### Preventing the Dialog from Closing

By default, dialogs will close when the user clicks the close button, clicks the overlay, or presses the [[Escape]] key. In most cases, the default behavior is the best behavior in terms of UX. However, there are situations where this may be undesirable, such as when data loss will occur.

To keep the dialog open in such cases, you can cancel the `sl-request-close` event. When canceled, the dialog will remain open and pulse briefly to draw the user's attention to it.

You can use `event.detail.source` to determine what triggered the request to close. This example prevents the dialog from closing when the overlay is clicked, but allows the close button or [[Escape]] to dismiss it.

```html
<sl-dialog label="Dialog" class="dialog-deny-close">
  This dialog will not close when you click on the overlay.
  <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Close</sl-button>
</sl-dialog>

<sl-button>Open Dialog</sl-button>

<script>
  const dialog = document.querySelector('.dialog-deny-close');
  const openButton = dialog.nextElementSibling;
  const closeButton = dialog.querySelector('sl-button[slot="footer"]');

  openButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.hide());

  // Prevent the dialog from closing when the user clicks on the overlay
  dialog.addEventListener('sl-request-close', event => {
    if (event.detail.source === 'overlay') {
      event.preventDefault();
    }
  });
</script>
```

```ts
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/button/button.js';
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/dialog/dialog.js';
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dialog-preventing-the-dialog-from-closing-example',
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <sl-dialog
      label="Dialog"
      [open]="open()"
      (sl-request-close)="handleRequestClose($event)"
      (sl-after-hide)="open.set(false)"
    >
      This dialog will not close when you click on the overlay.
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary" (click)="open.set(false)">Close</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-button (click)="open.set(true)">Open Dialog</sl-button>
  `
})
export class DialogPreventingTheDialogFromClosingExampleComponent {
  readonly open = signal(false);

  // sl-request-close is cancelable: preventing it keeps the dialog open and plays the "deny" animation.
  handleRequestClose(event: Event) {
    const { source } = (event as CustomEvent<{ source: 'close-button' | 'keyboard' | 'overlay' }>).detail;

    if (source === 'overlay') {
      event.preventDefault();
    }
  }
}
```

### Customizing Initial Focus

By default, the dialog's panel will gain focus when opened. This allows a subsequent tab press to focus on the first tabbable element in the dialog. If you want a different element to have focus, add the `autofocus` attribute to it as shown below.

```html
<sl-dialog label="Dialog" class="dialog-focus">
  <sl-input autofocus placeholder="I will have focus when the dialog is opened"></sl-input>
  <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary">Close</sl-button>
</sl-dialog>

<sl-button>Open Dialog</sl-button>

<script>
  const dialog = document.querySelector('.dialog-focus');
  const input = dialog.querySelector('sl-input');
  const openButton = dialog.nextElementSibling;
  const closeButton = dialog.querySelector('sl-button[slot="footer"]');

  openButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.hide());
</script>
```

```ts

import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/dialog/dialog.js';
import '@shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/input/input.js';
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dialog-customizing-initial-focus-example',
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <sl-dialog label="Dialog" [open]="open()" (sl-after-hide)="open.set(false)">
      <sl-input autofocus placeholder="I will have focus when the dialog is opened"></sl-input>
      <sl-button slot="footer" variant="primary" (click)="open.set(false)">Close</sl-button>
    </sl-dialog>

    <sl-button (click)="open.set(true)">Open Dialog</sl-button>
  `
})
export class DialogCustomizingInitialFocusExampleComponent {
  readonly open = signal(false);
}
```

> **Tip:** You can further customize initial focus behavior by canceling the `sl-initial-focus` event and setting focus yourself inside the event handler.
